[00:00] Avery (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm avery with redwood, i'll kick us off. can you all hear me okay?
[00:06] Riya (LatticeAI): yep, loud and clear — thanks, avery. excited to see the console, ben has been asking about per-route chargebacks.
[00:12] Ben (LatticeAI): yeah sorry, cut in — we need better visibility so finance can allocate costs to teams. current billing is fuzzy.
[00:18] Avery: totally. today's plan: quick context from you, then devon will walk the console live — per-route lenses, token-level breakdown, and the cost slice UI. then Q&A and next steps. sound good?
[00:26] Samir (LatticeAI): good for me. timeline: we're aiming to decide pilot by end of month.
[00:31] Riya: same. success metric is <10% regression vs current latency and 20% cost reduction target on top-3 routes.
[00:37] Devon (Redwood SE): cool, i'll share my screen in a sec. one note — couple of names may transcribe weirdly, i think the auto transcripts sometimes spell kvcache like K V cache.
[00:44] Ben: ha, yes we've seen that.
[00:46] [00:45] Devon: alright sharing screen — i'm in the Redwood Console, overview page. top-left is the usage heatmap, you can change the window to 1h/24h/30d. i'll jump to the "Routes" tab where we map usage per API route.
[00:58] Riya: quick q — routes here mean logical endpoints in our app, right? say /chat vs /summarize?
[01:04] Devon: exactly, they're the paths you send to the API. we ingest route metadata so you can tag by product, team, or environment.
[01:10] [01:10] Devon: ok i'm filtering to last 30 days, and showing two lenses: tokens and wall-time. look at this stacked bar — it shows route-level token consumption broken down by model variant. so you can see route X uses much more tokens on generation than route Y.
[01:23] Ben: I see — and that color legend ties back to model names? often our infra team cares about which model family costs the most.
[01:29] Devon: yes, that legend is model family. there are quick toggles to collapse model variants. also note the per-token cost estimate column: it's derived from your billing profile and the model/quantization profile.
[01:39] Riya: how accurate is that per-token cost? sometimes embeddings and chat tokens are priced differently.
[01:44] Devin: (laugh) i mean — so the console shows an estimated cost using your current pricing tier. if you have reserved dedicated capacity we pull committed rates; for hosted it's list rates with applied discounts. it's an estimate but aligns to invoice within a small margin unless you have custom pass-through tags.
[01:57] Samir: can we break down by prompt vs completion tokens? we need to know where to optimize.
[02:02] Devon: yep — there's a token breakdown view. switch to a route and open the detail pane — you'll see prompt/completion/hidden system tokens, and KV cache hits shown separately.
[02:12] Ben: KV cache hits are interesting — we do a lot of session-based reuse. can the console show cache hit ratio per route?
[02:18] Devon: yes, cache hit ratio appears in the route metrics and we surface the estimated token savings from those hits. you can also see suggestions from Optimize — for example, if cache hit is low we might suggest prefix caching or session pinning.
[02:30] Riya: nice. can you demo the cost-slice feature? that's the bit finance will love.
[02:35] Devon: sure — open 'Cost Slices' from the left nav. you can define a slice by route tag, model family, or time window. i'm creating a slice for team:assistant-service + model:llm-x -> and applying last 30 days.
[02:48] [02:47] Devon: the slice shows total tokens, estimated cost, p95 latency, and cost per 1K tokens. there's also a waterfall view that attributes cost to model inference, tokenization overhead, and network egress where applicable.
[03:00] Ben: waterfall view is super helpful. does egress show cloud provider egress or inter-region hops?
[03:05] Devon: if you're on Redwood Dedicated and we've instrumented your network tags, we surface provider egress. for hosted it's an estimate. we can integrate with your billing buckets for more precision during the pilot.
[03:14] Riya: security: we need SOC2, SSO, and KMS integration. how are audit logs surfaced?
[03:20] Avery: quick answer — yes, SOC2 and SSO/SAML are supported, KMS integrates for private deployments. audit logs are in the Console under Security -> Audit Logs, you can filter to API keys, route changes, rollout events. we'll send the SOC2 pack after this call.
[03:33] Samir: will audit logs include per-request metadata like user-agent or custom headers?
[03:37] Avery: we capture request-level metadata for retention windows you configure. some fields are redacted by default but you can opt-in if you need more.
[03:44] Ben: ok. about dedicated vs hosted: performance-wise what's typical for a 512-token average with p95 SLAs?
[03:51] Devon: on Dedicated with pinned GPUs we commonly hit p95 ~ 45-60ms for smaller models and ~120-180ms for larger families at moderate QPS. hosted may have slightly variable tail latencies but we have routing and fallbacks to keep things within SLA. exact numbers depend on batch sizes and KV cache effectiveness.
[04:08] Riya: that matches our target if caching does most of the heavy lifting. what about batching — can console suggest batching configs?
[04:14] Devon: yes Optimize will surface batching recommendations per route: target batch size, max latency budget, and expected cost savings. i can show an example for your chat route — it recommends batching window 12ms for that traffic pattern which should save ~18% on token cost.
[04:27] [04:25] Devon: switching to Insights -> Optimize suggestions. here's a list: batching, quantization profile (int8 vs int4 tradeoffs), and suggested model variant fallbacks for cost/latency.
[04:37] Samir: quantization — we need to know accuracy regression risk. does Optimize provide evals?
[04:41] Devon: yes, we tie suggestions to eval sets if you provide them. the UI shows expected regression and confidence bands — you can accept the quantization profile and run a canary rollout to a percent of traffic.
[04:53] Riya: about rollout — can we do canary per-route and automatic rollback on quality regression?
[04:58] Devon: exactly. rollout policies are per-route. you can set health checks tied to prompt sets and have automatic rollback if quality drops beyond threshold.
[05:07] Ben: ok, practical: for pilot we want three routes instrumented, run Optimize for two weeks and then compare costs. what's the onboarding effort?
[05:15] Avery: typical pilot is 2-3 weeks of integration: add SDK or route tags, point traffic, share sample logs. initial console visibility is immediate; Optimize suggestions arrive after 48–72 hours of traffic.
[05:27] Samir: do you need full production traffic or can we run mirrored traffic from staging?
[05:31] Devon: mirrored traffic works well for throughput and latency testing; for quality/regression you want real prompts.
[05:38] Riya: any limits on telemetry retention? we have requirements for 12 months.
[05:42] Avery: retention tiers are configurable — default 90 days, enterprise tier supports 12–24 months. we can outline retention pricing in the pack.
[05:50] Ben: competitors question — we evaluated openai + homegrown caching. how is redwood different from a self-hosted inference cluster?
[05:57] Devon: two big differences: first, the runtime is optimized for continuous batching and transparent kv cache sharing which cuts cost without much dev work; second, the Console + Optimize ties telemetry into concrete cost-saving recommendations and safe rollouts. you can replicate parts on your own but it takes significant engineering effort.
[06:15] [06:12] Riya: ok let's surface some edge-cases — we occasionally have bursty traffic: can routing move traffic to cheaper model variants automatically?
[06:20] Devon: yes policy-based routing supports latency or cost thresholds and will fallback to compatible variants. you can set global fallbacks or per-route.
[06:28] Samir: any GDPR/residency concerns? we need EU data residency for EU users.
[06:33] Avery: supported in Private and Dedicated deployments; hosted offers region pinning but for hard residency you likely want Private or Dedicated with contract terms.
[06:42] Ben: one last technical — will Optimize suggestions include mixed-precision or kernel-level options for our GPU?
[06:48] Devon: suggestions include quantization profile and recommended kernel sets. for Dedicated we'll correlate with your GPU type and recommend best runtime flags.
[06:56] Riya: great. can we get sample dashboards for our CFO to review? he wants clear charts not engineering graphs.
[07:02] Avery: yes we have a finance view template — cost by team, top routes by spend, forecasted monthly spend by model family. i'll attach that template to follow-up email.
[07:12] Ben: timeline recap: we'll share sample traffic and route list; you (redwood) send pricing and SOC2 docs; then schedule pilot kickoff.
[07:20] Avery: correct — action items we'll capture and send. any other questions?
[07:25] Samir: none from me. thanks for the demo.
[07:28] Riya: no more. thanks everyone.
